name: Accessibility

hero.title: One line, and screen readers hear “Saved”.
hero.lede: `announce('Saved')` speaks to screen-reader users from anywhere in your app, with no provider and nothing to mount. Add a signal-driven live region, a skip link, visually hidden labels and ARIA ids: the pieces single-page apps usually leave out.

why.title: The accessibility gaps SPAs leave open, closed.

items.title: Say what just happened
items.text: "Saved", "3 results", "Connection lost". `announce()` writes into a polite or assertive live region it created on first use. Two messages in the same moment are joined, not overwritten, and saying "Saved" twice is heard twice.

items.title: Status that announces itself
items.text: `<LiveRegion>{() => status()}</LiveRegion>` speaks every change of a signal. No effect, no call. It renders on the server, so the region exists before the first update after hydration.

items.title: Navigation you can hear
items.text: In a single-page app the page never reloads, so a screen reader stays silent. The root `<RouterView>` announces each new page by default; `<RouteAnnouncer>` lets you choose the wording.

items.title: The same call on the phone
items.text: Compiled for iOS (native targets are experimental), `announce()` becomes a VoiceOver announcement; on Android the compiler hosts polite and assertive live regions for TalkBack. Politeness carries over on both (iOS 17 and later).

before.label: by hand
before.caption: A live region you mount, clear and refill on a timer, or a repeat goes unheard.
before.code: function save() { // … const el = document.getElementById('status')! el.textContent = '' setTimeout(() => { el.textContent = 'Settings saved' }, 100) }

after.label: with @pyreon/a11y
after.caption: One call, from any handler. The regions, the clearing and the repeat handling are done for you.
after.code:
import { announce } from '@pyreon/a11y'

announce('Settings saved')
announce('Connection lost', { politeness: 'assertive' })
announce('Copied', { clearAfter: 1000 })

limits.title: Keep assertive for what is urgent
limits.text: An assertive message cuts off whatever the user was hearing. Use it for errors and lost connections; leave status updates polite.

limits.title: Announcements happen in the browser
limits.text: `announce()` does nothing during SSR, by design. Call it from handlers and effects, not while rendering.

limits.title: One route announcer at a time
limits.text: `<RouterView>` already announces navigation. If you add `<RouteAnnouncer>`, switch the built-in one off; a dev warning tells you when both are running.

limits.title: clearAfter stays on the web
limits.text: In native builds `announce()` keeps its politeness, but `clearAfter` is ignored on iOS and Android.

recipes.title: Search results a screen reader can count
recipes.text: A visible result count that is also announced every time it changes. `<LiveRegion>` tracks the computed, so there is no announce call to remember.

recipes.title: A field that explains itself
recipes.text: The hint is linked to the input with a generated id, the input flags itself invalid, and the outcome is spoken: assertive for the error, polite for success.

recipes.title: Your own words for every page
recipes.text: A skip link first in the tab order, and route changes announced as "Billing page". Turn the router's built-in announcer off when you use your own, or every page is announced twice.

faq.q: Do I need to mount a provider or an announcer component?
faq.a: No. The first `announce()` call creates two visually hidden live regions on `document.body`, one polite (`role="status"`) and one assertive (`role="alert"`), and reuses them for the life of the page.

faq.q: Why does a message arrive about 100 ms after the call?
faq.a: Screen readers often ignore a live region that is created and filled in the same moment, and rapid writes overwrite each other. The short wait lets the region exist first and lets messages sent together be joined into one announcement.
`announce()` for one-off events with no place in the layout, like "Copied". `<LiveRegion>` when the status already lives somewhere on the page, like a result count or a "Saving…" line.

faq.q: Do I need `<RouteAnnouncer>` with the Pyreon router?
faq.a: Usually not: the root `<RouterView>` announces route changes on its own. Use `<RouteAnnouncer>` for custom wording or politeness, and pass `announceRouteChanges={false}` to `<RouterView>` when you do.

faq.q: Does this replace an accessibility audit?
faq.a: No. These are building blocks. For checks, Atlas runs axe-core on each generated component scenario, and `@pyreon/lint` has opt-in rules such as `pyreon/require-img-alt` and `pyreon/no-positive-tabindex`.
